description: IDA* (Iterative Deepening A*) finds a cheapest path with an *admissible* heuristic `h` (one that never overestimates), in memory linear in the path length. It runs a series of depth-first searches, and each search prunes a state when `f = g + h` exceeds a threshold. The first threshold is `h` of the start; each next threshold is the smallest `f` that the last search pruned. IDA* keeps only the current path, so it expands a state again in every iteration and along every path that reaches it. Use it on trees and on graphs where few paths lead to the same state and few distinct `f` values occur; many distinct float costs mean many iterations.

papers.title: Depth-first iterative-deepening: An optimal admissible tree search

lineage.source: Depth-first iterative-deepening: An optimal admissible tree search, Section 6: "Depth-first iterative-deepening can also be combined with a best-first heuristic"
